articles.title: How to Build Judgement about a New Technology or Business
articles.content:
每个月，巧克力牛奶教派（Chocolate Milk Cult）可触及超过百万名建设者、创业者、投资者、政策制定者和领导者等。如果您想认识我们社区的其他成员，请填写以下联系表格（我不会出售您的数据，也不会在未经您明确许可的情况下进行介绍）——[联系表格链接](https://forms.gle/Pi1pGLuS1FmzXoLr6)。

大约一周前，我收到了一位非常富有的投资者提供的百万美元职位邀请。他们一直在阅读这份新闻通讯，对我们涵盖的主题范围感到印象深刻。模型架构、基础设施、硬件、经济学、公司战略，以及我有时在写作之前从未涉足过的技术领域（例如关于Weka和AI中内存瓶颈的深度探讨）——
投资者最感兴趣的是速度。我如何能够在短时间内阅读和理解许多不同领域的内容，并建立足够深入的认知地图，从而定期撰写深度分析？是的，人工智能有所帮助，但他们想了解如何有效利用人工智能来评估多个新兴行业并做出相应预测。

这篇文章将揭示这一过程。

许多人在试图理解新技术时浪费了大量时间。他们从论文、术语、架构、基准测试和实施细节入手。几周后，他们了解了很多，但可能仍无法回答那些关键问题。

在我看来，知识的核心在于决策力：在能够用于做出有意义的决策来推进你的议程时，它才最有用。这意味着你必须能够快速回答以下问题：
- 为什么这种技术现在出现？
- 它解决了什么限制？
- 谁从中受益？
- 什么可能阻碍它成功？
- 它是否改变了足够重要的事情，以至于你需要采取行动？

这些问题告诉我哪些技术细节值得关注，哪些可以暂时忽略。

这形成了一个迭代过程。你学习足够多的知识以形成初步观点。这个观点会告诉你不确定性在哪里。然后，你只在解决这些不确定性可能改变你的决策的地方进行深入研究。这个过程能建立更具记忆性和可操作性的理解。

About a week ago, I was offered a multimillion-dollar role by a very wealthy investor. They had been reading this newsletter and were impressed by the range of subjects we cover. Model architecture, infrastructure, hardware, economics, company strategy, and technical areas I had sometimes never worked on before writing about them (such as this deep dive into Weka and the memory bottleneck in AI)—

More than anything else, they were interested in the speed. How was I able to read so much about very different fields, and build a deep enough map to write deep dives on them so regularly? Yes AI helps, but they wnated to know how to use it most effectively to be able to assess multiple emerging industries and make predictions accordingly.

This article is a breakdown that process.

Most people waste enormous amounts of time when they try to understand a new technology. They begin with papers, terminology, architectures, benchmarks, and implementation details. Weeks later, they know a lot more, but they may still be unable to answer the basic questions that matter.

To me, knowledge is about decision making power: it’s most useful when you can use it to make meaningfully decisions to move your agenda. This means tha you have to be able to answer questions such as

  • Why does this technology exist now?

  • What constraint does it remove?

  • Who benefits from it?

  • What could prevent it from succeeding?

  • Does it change anything important enough for you to act?

and many others quickly so you can make the important decisions. Such questions tell me which technical details deserve attention and which ones can be ignored for now.

This creates an iterative process. You learn enough to form an initial view. That view tells you where the uncertainty is. You then go deeper only where resolving that uncertainty could change your decision. This process builds a much memorable (and more actionable) understanding of what you’re studying.
